_note: Fixture content for a scripted run, written by one author. It exercises the mechanics and includes deliberate violations for the gates to catch. It has none of the independence of a model-backed run.

body.text: Is the registry the problem, or undeclared coupling? If every consumer used a client generated from a pinned contract, most breakage would show up at build time without a registry service.
body.reframe: How do we make every cross-repo dependency declared, pinned and checked, so a breaking change is caught where it happens?

body.title: Consumer expectations first
body.summary: Each consumer publishes expectation tests for the fields and behaviour it relies on. A producer change runs every consumer's tests before merge (can-i-deploy). The registry stores contracts, consumers and their tests.

body.text: Consumers will keep their expectation tests current
body.test: Count expectation tests updated per contract change over two weeks of agent work

body.text: Expectation tests catch semantic changes when they assert example values
body.test: Mutation test: change a unit in an example and confirm a consumer test fails

body.title: Schema-diff gate in CI
body.summary: Contracts live as files in the control repo. CI runs oasdiff, buf breaking or JSON Schema compatibility on every change and routes breaking ones by decision rights. The registry is an index of files and owners.

body.text: Structural diffs catch most breaking changes in our engagements
body.test: Replay the last 20 interface changes and count breaks the diff misses

body.title: Generated clients, no registry service
body.summary: Consumers generate clients from the producer's contract at a pinned version, so undeclared usage fails at build time. A contract bump is an ordinary basis change the Observator already tracks.

body.title: Weekly contract review
body.summary: A standing review of all interface changes once a week.

body.title: Semantic contracts with examples
body.summary: Design-first contracts carry units, invariants and worked examples. Consumers pin a version and generate clients. Any change to semantics or examples counts as breaking until every consumer's example-based tests pass.

body.text: Agents will write semantic annotations and examples for each contract
body.test: Check the next 10 contracts written by agents for units, invariants and examples

body.title: Monorepo per engagement
body.summary: Put an engagement's repos in one monorepo so interface changes are atomic commits. Keep a registry only for client-owned interfaces.

body.text: Clients will accept a monorepo per engagement
body.test: Ask the owners of the two active engagements

body.title: Lighter semantic contracts
body.summary: Like the risk angle's idea, minus the examples.

body.text: Hand-written expectation tests are a maintenance cost on every consumer; tests generated from contract examples avoid most of it.

body.title: Existing tools behind a thin registry
body.summary: Use schema-diff tools and consumer-driven tests as they are. The registry stores only pointers, owners and pins, so there's nothing new to maintain.

body.text: Existing tools can run inside each engagement's walls without a shared broker
body.test: Run one engagement's contract tests with no network access to other engagements

body.text: Pointers and owners don't tell a consumer what changed for them; someone still has to read a diff before acting.
body.test: Show three consumers a pointer-only change notice and ask whether they can act on it

body.text: Unit changes slip through schema diffs.
Hand-written expectation tests rot, and every consumer carries the cost.
body.test: Count expectation tests updated per contract change over two weeks

body.text: Structural diffs miss semantic changes: a unit switch keeps the schema identical.
Client-owned repos often can't merge into a monorepo, so this fails exactly where breakage hurts most.
body.test: Ask the owners of the two active engagements

body.text: Our annotations might drift.
Any shared broker crosses client walls.
Annotations nobody executes drift from the code; examples must run as tests or they rot.
body.test: Mutation test: change a unit in an example and confirm a consumer test fails

body.text: Consumer tests generated from contract examples catch unit changes that schema diffs miss
body.test: Mutation test: change a unit in one example and confirm the generated consumer test fails

body.text: Treating every semantic or example change as breaking won't flood owners with briefs
body.test: Replay a month of contract changes and count the escalations

body.text: Contract files in the control repo can be pinned like any other basis
body.test: Pin one contract in a lockfile and bump it

body.text: Consumers will review expectation tests weekly
